Car registration and driver licence after a death in Queensland

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 9 Nov 2026

A Queensland vehicle registered in two names can be transferred free of charge to the surviving registered operator with proof of death and original evidence of identity. Otherwise the executor, administrator or next of kin transfers or cancels the registration with TMR form F5296 and either the grant of probate or letters of administration, the will (for an executor) or a statutory declaration (for next of kin). A beneficiary usually must survive the deceased by 30 days first. The driver licence can be surrendered, with a refund of the licence fee, at a transport and motoring service centre or by mail with form F4778.

Key facts

  • Joint registration: free transfer to the survivor
  • Otherwise form F5296 with probate, will or statutory declaration
  • 30-day survival period for beneficiaries
  • Licence refund via service centre or form F4778

What are the steps?

  1. Expect a letter. When TMR learns of a death (from Births, Deaths and Marriages or the next of kin) it writes to the last known address listing vehicles and personalised or customised plates to transfer or cancel, and places a restriction on them. The registration isn't cancelled, but it can't be renewed until it's transferred.
  2. Jointly registered vehicle: the surviving registered operator can transfer it into their name free of charge with proof of death (if no Registration Notice Individual Restriction letter has been received) and original evidence of identity. No other forms are needed.
  3. Otherwise, work out your authority. With a grant of probate or letters of administration, present the original or certified copies with form F5296; you don't need the will, the death certificate or the statutory declaration. If probate or administration has been applied for but not yet granted, wait for the grant.
  4. No grant? An executor named in the last valid will presents the original or a certified copy of the will and completes F5296 including the statutory declaration. With no will, the next of kin (under the Succession Act 1981) completes F5296 including the statutory declaration.
  5. TMR may ask for the original or a certified copy of the death certificate or coroner's report.
  6. To transfer or cancel: complete any extra forms listed on F5296, present original evidence of identity and pay any fees. Unattached customised plates must be cancelled. Where there are several executors or administrators, only one needs to sign and present ID.
  7. Not ready to decide? Transfer the registration temporarily into the estate, with the executor, administrator or next of kin as the second registered operator responsible for the vehicle.
  8. Driver licence: surrender it and claim a refund of the licence fee at a transport and motoring service centre with the licence (unless lost or destroyed) and one supporting document: death certificate, coroner's report, Public Trustee certificate of authority, sealed grant of probate, or advice from Births, Deaths and Marriages. Originals, or copies certified by a JP or other qualified person.
  9. By mail: send the return/surrender declaration form F4778, the licence and a certified copy of the supporting document to TMR, Emerald Customer Service Centre, PO Box 1787, Emerald QLD 4720. The refund is a cheque in the name of the licensee or their estate and can take up to 15 working days.

Frequently asked questions

What happens to car registration when the owner dies in Queensland?

TMR places a restriction on vehicles and plates in the deceased's name and writes to their last known address. The registration isn't cancelled, but it can't be renewed until it's transferred to an eligible person or entity.

Can I transfer a deceased person's car before probate in Queensland?

If probate or letters of administration have been applied for, TMR says you can't finalise the registration until they're granted. If no grant is being sought, an executor can use the will, or the next of kin a statutory declaration, with form F5296. You can also transfer it temporarily into the estate.

How do I transfer a jointly registered car after a death?

The surviving registered operator can transfer it into their name free of charge with proof of death and original evidence of identity. No other forms are needed.

What is the 30-day survival period?

In most cases a beneficiary must survive the deceased by at least 30 days before receiving benefits under the will, so TMR says not to apply to transfer the registration in that time unless the will says otherwise or you're transferring it into the 'estate of' the deceased.

How do I cancel a deceased person's Queensland driver licence?

Surrender it at a transport and motoring service centre, or by mail with form F4778, with a supporting document such as the death certificate. You can apply for a refund of the licence fee, paid by cheque to the licensee or their estate within about 15 working days.

What about personalised plates?

Personalised or customised plates in the deceased's name must be transferred or cancelled along with the registration, and unattached customised plates must be cancelled.
